speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a significant medical history; could you please tell me specifically what conditions you have been diagnosed with in the past? Additionally, how long have you been experiencing the gait and limb ataxia?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any memory loss, vision changes, or trouble speaking, and do you have a history of multiple sclerosis or a previous stroke? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain Findings: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). Comments: T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Patient
text: The walking difficulty and coordination problems are the main issues. I do not have chest pain or other major symptoms besides the neurological problems. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful, but since you mentioned a previous doctor suggested Multiple Sclerosis, have you ever had an MRI or spinal tap to confirm it? REQUEST TEST: MRI Spine with contrast. REQUEST IMAGES: Previous MRI Brain if available.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS (No data provided for MRI Spine with contrast or previous MRI Brain images in the available records).

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRI results are normal, which makes Multiple Sclerosis highly unlikely despite the suggestion, have you noticed any numbness, tingling, or weakness specifically on the right side of your body? Also, do you have a history of head trauma or a family history of movement disorders? REQUEST TEST: Lumbar_Puncture; REQUEST TEST: Serum_Anti-GQ1b_and_Anti-Yo_ antibodies.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal MRI and antibody results, and your history of ataxia worsening after a period of stability, have you noticed any episodes where your speech became slurred or your eyes moved rapidly in one direction? REQUEST TEST: Serum_Anti-NMDA_receptor_antibodies; REQUEST TEST: Serum_Anti-LGI1_antibodies.
